correctness.rationale: The Desargues graph is defined without ambiguity as the incidence graph of 2- and 3-subsets of [5]. Exhaustive graph distances agree pairwise with symmetric-difference distance; the exact lists of nonempty simplices have f-vectors (20,90,120,30) at scale 2 and (20,150,540,1000,960,450,80) at scale 3. The standalone deterministic verifier executes and verifies the unique free coface of all 30 and 1040 elementary simplicial collapse pairs respectively. A spanning-tree/triangle quotient kills every generator of pi1 at scale 2 in five rounds, and all scale-three edges are homotopic to scale-two paths, proving pi1=0 there. An exact integral 540-by-410 tetrahedral boundary matrix is reduced using 409 invertible integer unit pivots to one zero column, certifying rank 409, primitiveness of the image, and H3=Z with H2=0 and no torsion. The 3-dimensional core and Hurewicz/Whitehead imply homotopy S3. At scale 4 the unique ten forbidden antipodal pairs imply a tenfold S0 join, S9. At other scales the graph rank and diameter suffice. All four bar degrees are disjoint at adjacent stages. This is full finite verification plus rigorous topology, not sampling or extrapolation.

originality.rationale: Feng and Nukala Theorem 13 ALREADY proves the scale-two term for this same 2/3-subset metric (19 copies S2), which is expressly identified as prior work, not counted as new. Their entire paper concerns scale two and Section 7 points to the gap at larger scales. The additional scale-three equivalence to the Petersen prism independence complex and homotopy S3, coupled with complete barcode, are not implied by their theorem. Saleh, Titz Mite and Witzel classify only Platonic-solid vertex sets; their different 20-vertex cubic dodecahedral graph instead has 9 S3 at scale three. Adamaszek and Adams study finite subsets of circles, not this incidence graph. Carnero Bravo focuses on path categorical/strong products rather than the Cartesian Petersen prism. Research-record semantic searches for aliases and exact parameters found related graph complexes but no covering claim. Residual risk of obscure equivalent prism calculation is acknowledged.
residual_risks: No claim of an exhaustive search of unpublished or unindexed equivalences; an unlocated general independence-complex theorem could subsume the Petersen prism.

value.rationale: This canonical (10_3) incidence graph has 20 vertices, 30 edges and five distinct graph-metric distances. Its complete persistent topology has four positive homology dimensions: 1,2,3,9. The scale-three term links the Desargues metric space to the independent-set topology of the Petersen prism, and its one-dimensional integral top class is far from the nine corresponding classes in the equally sized dodecahedral graph. A complete exact barcode and homotopy model of such a natural finite graph are motivated, nontrivial structural invariants; there is no arbitrary unmotivated parameter slice, nor is a general theorem asserted.
